messages.author: 238422c6037ad1c9
messages.subject: rgenerica - DAGAR model
parts:
Dear all, 
Thank you very much in advance for your time. I am trying to fir a Spatial DAGAR model (Datta, A 2018) in generic, and with your help in the previous post I had come out with this code that unfortunately is giving me this error message: 

GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE

 Attach is the function for the DAGAR specification in case of interest. 
Is there any special reason why the model is not converging, maybe something wrong with the code?

Thank you in advance!

Datta, A., Banerjee, S., Hodges, J. S., & Gao, L. (2018). Spatial disease mapping using directed acyclic graph auto-regressive (DAGAR) models. Bayesian Analysis.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] rgenerica - DAGAR model
parts:
I would recommend to test this out using

inla.rgeneric.q

so that you can test that your rgeneric definition is doing the right
thing. check that the graph is correct, the precision matrix is correct
and pos definite, etc...

also, I would recommend to pass 'num' and 'adj' as arguments in
rgeneric.define, so you do not need to evaluate them at every call to
DAGAR.function.

Here, the dimension is small, but in general, you would have to
construct the matrices using sparse format, instead of using dense
matrices that is converted to sparse later one. well, it have nothing
to do if this is correct or not, just the speed.

H
